question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q2b — Specific Heat Capacity Calculation
question.text:
A group of students used an electrical method to calculate the specific heat capacity of a liquid.

  • Time for heating: 400 s
  • Mass of liquid: 0.2 kg
  • Initial temperature: 25°C
  • Final temperature: 70°C
  • Energy supplied by immersion heater: 15.6 kJ

Assume no heat was lost and ignore the heat capacity of the container.
question.general_feedback:
Part (ii) — Specific heat capacity:
ΔT = 70 − 25 = 45°C
E = 15.6 kJ = 15 600 J
c = E / (m × ΔT) = 15 600 / (0.2 × 45) = 15 600 / 9 = 1 733 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹

Part (iii) — Power rating:
P = E / t = 15 600 / 400 = 39 W

Common error in (ii): using ΔT = 70 without subtracting initial temperature, or forgetting to convert kJ → J.

steps.label:
Given: t = 400 s  |  m = 0.2 kg  |  θ₁ = 25°C  |  θ₂ = 70°C  |  E = 15.6 kJ
Formulas: c = E / (m × ΔT)    P = E / t
Note: convert kJ to J (× 1000) before substituting.
Part (ii) — Calculate the specific heat capacity of the liquid. (5 marks)
Part (iii) — Calculate the power rating of the immersion heater. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: ΔT = θ₂ − θ₁ = 70 − 25 = 45°C. You must subtract the initial temperature, not use the final temperature alone.
1 kJ = 1000 J, so 15.6 kJ = 15 600 J. Did you multiply by 1000?

fields.label: Specific heat capacity c = _____ J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Specific heat capacity formula: c = E / (m × ΔT). Rearrange the formula Q = mcΔT to make c the subject.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Did you use ΔT = 45 (not 70)? And E = 15 600 J (not 15.6)? Substitute carefully: 15 600 ÷ (0.2 × 45).

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: P = E ÷ t = 15 600 ÷ 400 = 39 W. Use energy in joules (15 600 J) and time in seconds (400 s).
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Power formula: P = E / t (energy divided by time). The unit is watts (W = J/s).
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The same energy (15 600 J) is used here as in part (ii). P = 15 600 ÷ 400 = 39 W.
